title: The healing power of singing
paragraphs: From singing at concerts to singing 'Happy birthday'. Around the world, humans have been singing in unison for millennia. Some anthropologists even think our ancestors may have sung before they could speak. "Lullabies are sung to children, and then songs are sung at funerals", says Alex Street, from the Cambridge Institute for Music Therapy Research, who thinks that our positive response to music is no accident. Music is not only enjoyable, but beneficial for our health.

There is growing evidence that singing can energise us, improve immune function and increase feelings of happiness, according to 'A Review of the Physiological Effects and Mechanisms of Singing', published in 2018. It's thought that the repeated and controlled breathing that singing requires releases endorphins, which are chemicals released by the brain associated with pleasure and wellbeing. It may even provide a physical workout comparable to a brisk walk. And singing as part of a group or choir may have additional effects. Researchers in 'The icebreaker effect: singing mediates fast social bonding' found that singing together accelerated faster social cohesion among strangers.

Some studies have also found that regular musical activity can help to delay the onset of various neurological conditions such as Parkinson's disease and dementia. And it's not too late for those already living with such conditions. Cathy McGlynn is a music therapist based in Ireland who leads a choir of people with Parkinson's. The disease can lead to respiratory and vocal problems, both of which are benefited by singing practice. For those suffering with dementia, singing can enhance the type of memory which helps us recall names and specific personal experiences, according to a literature review on singing and cognitive health called 'A Song for the Mind'. Music therapist Grace Meadows watched as a woman with dementia got up out of her chair and started dancing at a musical performance. "It was the first time the carers had ever seen her move, unaided."

Music may not be a medicine in the traditional sense, but one thing seems clear: humans are wired for connection, and music helps to create it. So, if you're sceptical about the power of music, it may be time to change your tune.
chineseParagraphs: 从在音乐会唱歌到唱“生日快乐”歌。世界各地，人类齐声歌唱已有数千年历史。一些人类学家甚至认为我们的祖先在会说话之前可能就已经会唱歌了。“摇篮曲是唱给孩子的，而葬礼上也会唱歌，”剑桥音乐治疗研究所的亚历克斯·斯特里特说，他认为我们对音乐的积极反应并非偶然。音乐不仅令人愉悦，而且对我们的健康有益。
根据2018年发表的《歌唱的生理效应与机制回顾》，越来越多的证据表明，唱歌可以让我们充满活力，改善免疫功能，并增加幸福感。人们认为，唱歌所需的重复且有控制的呼吸会释放内啡肽，这是大脑释放的与愉悦和幸福相关的化学物质。它甚至可能提供相当于快走的身体锻炼。而作为团体或合唱团的一部分进行唱歌可能还有额外效果。《破冰效应：唱歌促进快速社会联系》的研究人员发现，一起唱歌能加速陌生人群之间的社会凝聚力。

一些研究还发现，定期的音乐活动有助于延缓帕金森病和痴呆等多种神经系统疾病的发作。对于已经患有这些疾病的人来说，现在开始也为时不晚。凯西·麦格林是爱尔兰的一名音乐治疗师，她领导着一个由帕金森病患者组成的合唱团。这种疾病可能导致呼吸和发声问题，而唱歌练习对这两方面都有益处。根据一篇关于唱歌和认知健康的文献综述《心灵的歌声》，对于痴呆症患者，唱歌可以增强那种帮助我们回忆名字和特定个人经历的记忆类型。音乐治疗师格蕾丝·梅多斯曾目睹一位患有痴呆症的女士在一场音乐表演中从椅子上站起来开始跳舞。“这是护理人员第一次看到她无需帮助就能自己活动。”
音乐可能不是传统意义上的药物，但有一点似乎很清楚：人类天生就为联系而生，而音乐有助于创造这种联系。所以，如果你对音乐的力量持怀疑态度，也许是时候改变你的看法了。

vocabulary.entry: in unison /ɪn ˈjuːnɪsn/ phr. 一致地，齐声（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The audience sang in unison at the concert.
vocabulary.translation: 观众在音乐会上齐声歌唱。

vocabulary.entry: millennia /mɪˈleniə/ n. 数千年（millennium的复数，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Civilization has existed for millennia.
vocabulary.translation: 文明已经存在了数千年。

vocabulary.entry: anthropologist /ˌænθrəˈpɒlədʒɪst/ n. 人类学家（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The anthropologist studied indigenous tribes in the Amazon.
vocabulary.translation: 这位人类学家研究了亚马逊的土著部落。

vocabulary.entry: ancestor /ˈænsestə(r)/ n. 祖先，祖宗
vocabulary.example: His ancestors came from Ireland.
vocabulary.translation: 他的祖先来自爱尔兰。

vocabulary.entry: lullaby /ˈlʌləbaɪ/ n. 摇篮曲
vocabulary.example: She sang a lullaby to put the baby to sleep.
vocabulary.translation: 她唱摇篮曲哄宝宝入睡。

vocabulary.entry: funeral /ˈfjuːnərəl/ n. 葬礼
vocabulary.example: The funeral will be held on Saturday.
vocabulary.translation: 葬礼将于周六举行。

vocabulary.definition: 治疗师，心理治疗师（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: therapist /ˈθerəpɪst/ n. 治疗师，心理治疗师（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She sees a therapist once a week for anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 她每周去看一次心理治疗师治疗焦虑。

vocabulary.definition: 生理的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: physiological /ˌfɪziəˈlɒdʒɪkl/ adj. 生理的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The study examined the physiological effects of stress.
vocabulary.translation: 这项研究考察了压力的生理影响。

vocabulary.entry: mechanism /ˈmekənɪzəm/ n. 机制，原理（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The mechanism of action of the drug is not fully understood.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药物的作用机制尚未完全了解。

vocabulary.definition: 内啡肽（生物化学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: endorphin /enˈdɔːfɪn/ n. 内啡肽（生物化学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Exercise releases endorphins that make you feel good.
vocabulary.translation: 运动释放内啡肽，让你感觉良好。

vocabulary.entry: workout /ˈwɜːkaʊt/ n. 锻炼，训练（口语）
vocabulary.example: She does a 30-minute workout every morning.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天早上锻炼30分钟。

vocabulary.definition: 可与……相比的，类似的（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: comparable to /ˈkɒmpərəbl tu/ phr. 可与……相比的，类似的（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The two systems are comparable in terms of performance.
vocabulary.translation: 这两个系统在性能方面是可比的。

vocabulary.entry: brisk /brɪsk/ adj. 轻快的，敏捷的
vocabulary.example: He walked at a brisk pace.
vocabulary.translation: 他轻快地走着。

vocabulary.entry: choir /ˈkwaɪə(r)/ n. 合唱团，唱诗班
vocabulary.example: She sings in the school choir.
vocabulary.translation: 她在学校合唱团唱歌。

vocabulary.definition: 破冰者，打破僵局的事物（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: icebreaker /ˈaɪsbreɪkə(r)/ n. 破冰者，打破僵局的事物（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: They played an icebreaker game to get to know each other.
vocabulary.translation: 他们玩了一个破冰游戏来相互了解。

vocabulary.entry: mediate /ˈmiːdieɪt/ v. 调解，促成（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The therapist mediated the conversation between the two parties.
vocabulary.translation: 治疗师促成了双方的对话。

vocabulary.definition: 社会凝聚力（专业术语，固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: social cohesion /ˈsəʊʃl kəʊˈhiːʒn/ n. 社会凝聚力（专业术语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Shared activities can strengthen social cohesion.
vocabulary.translation: 共享活动可以加强社会凝聚力。

vocabulary.entry: delay /dɪˈleɪ/ v. 延迟，推迟
vocabulary.example: The flight was delayed due to bad weather.
vocabulary.translation: 航班因天气恶劣而延误。

vocabulary.entry: onset /ˈɒnset/ n. 开始，发病（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The onset of the disease is usually gradual.
vocabulary.translation: 这种疾病的发病通常是渐进的。

vocabulary.definition: 神经学的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: neurological /ˌnjʊərəˈlɒdʒɪkl/ adj. 神经学的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The patient has a neurological condition affecting his mobility.
vocabulary.translation: 病人有一种影响其活动能力的神经系统疾病。

vocabulary.definition: 帕金森病（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: Parkinson's disease /ˈpɑːkɪnsnz dɪziːz/ n. 帕金森病（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Parkinson's disease is a neurodegenerative disorder.
vocabulary.translation: 帕金森病是一种神经退行性疾病。

vocabulary.entry: dementia /dɪˈmenʃə/ n. 痴呆（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The hospital has a special unit for patients with dementia.
vocabulary.translation: 这家医院有一个专门收治痴呆症患者的病房。

vocabulary.definition: 呼吸的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: respiratory /rəˈspɪrətri/ adj. 呼吸的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Smoking can cause respiratory problems.
vocabulary.translation: 吸烟会导致呼吸系统问题。

vocabulary.entry: vocal /ˈvəʊkl/ adj. 声音的，有声的
vocabulary.example: She has a great vocal range.
vocabulary.translation: 她的音域很广。

vocabulary.entry: recall /rɪˈkɔːl/ v. 回忆，回想（书面语）
vocabulary.example: I can't recall her name at the moment.
vocabulary.translation: 我现在想不起她的名字。

vocabulary.definition: 文献综述（学术术语，固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: literature review /ˈlɪtrətʃə rɪˈvjuː/ n. 文献综述（学术术语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The researcher conducted a literature review on the topic.
vocabulary.translation: 研究人员对该主题进行了文献综述。

vocabulary.definition: 无辅助的，独立的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: unaided /ʌnˈeɪdɪd/ adj. 无辅助的，独立的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She can now walk unaided.
vocabulary.translation: 她现在可以独立行走了。

vocabulary.entry: medicine /ˈmedɪsn/ n. 药物，医学
vocabulary.example: This new medicine may help treat the disease.
vocabulary.translation: 这种新药可能有助于治疗这种疾病。

vocabulary.definition: 从传统意义上说（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: in the traditional sense /ɪn ðə trəˈdɪʃənl sens/ phr. 从传统意义上说（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: It's not a museum in the traditional sense.
vocabulary.translation: 从传统意义上说，这不是一个博物馆。

vocabulary.definition: 天生适合，有……的倾向（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: be wired for /biː ˈwaɪəd fɔː(r)/ phr. 天生适合，有……的倾向（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Humans are wired for social connection.
vocabulary.translation: 人类天生就适合社交联系。

vocabulary.entry: sceptical /ˈskeptɪkl/ adj. 怀疑的（英式）（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Many people are sceptical about the benefits of the new drug.
vocabulary.translation: 许多人对这种新药的好处持怀疑态度。

vocabulary.definition: 改变看法/态度（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: change your tune /ˌtʃeɪndʒ jɔː ˈtjuːn/ phr. 改变看法/态度（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: He changed his tune when he heard the evidence.
vocabulary.translation: 听到证据后他改变了看法。
